psa.title: PSA Nitrogen Generation System for Laser Cutting | GasMixTech
psa.description: Configure complete or modular PSA nitrogen generation for laser cutting around required flow, purity, pressure, operating hours and existing plant equipment.
psa.product_name: PSA Nitrogen Generation System for Laser Cutting
psa.category: On-site nitrogen supply for laser cutting
psa.h1: PSA nitrogen generation configured around your cutting demand
psa.lede: A complete or modular nitrogen supply for laser cutting plants that want to generate nitrogen on site and retain the equipment that already works.
psa.hero_note: Project-configured · Pure-nitrogen or mixed-gas workflows · No direct online purchase
psa.visual_alt: Complete PSA nitrogen generation process from compressed air to boosted nitrogen storage
psa.visual_caption: COMPLETE SYSTEM PATH · COMPRESSED AIR TO HIGH-PRESSURE N₂
psa.fit_title: An optional upstream nitrogen source—not a mandatory part of every project
psa.fit_text: Use the PSA system for pure nitrogen cutting, or as the upstream nitrogen source for one selected N₂/O₂ mixer. Plants with a suitable liquid, bulk or cylinder nitrogen supply can use that source instead.
psa.route_aria: PSA nitrogen system relationship to laser cutting and mixed-gas control
psa.reference_title: Two reference configurations for project discussion
psa.reference_text: These are the two configurations supported by the current source documents. They are reference configurations, not a claim that every site will use the same package.
psa.scope_title: Specify the full line, then decide which modules are actually supplied
psa.scope_text: The engineering review starts with the complete gas path. The supply scope is then reduced or expanded according to the customer’s existing compressor, air treatment, tanks and booster.

cards.title: Air compression
cards.text: Screw compressor and air buffer capacity are checked against flow and duty cycle.

cards.title: Air purification
cards.text: Drying and staged filtration protect the adsorption process and downstream gas quality.

cards.title: PSA generation
cards.text: Twin-tower adsorption separates nitrogen from compressed air for the required process demand.

cards.title: Buffer and storage
cards.text: Process and storage vessels stabilize supply around the selected operating profile.

cards.title: Pressure boosting
cards.text: A nitrogen booster raises pressure when the cutting process or downstream mixer requires it.
cards.meta: Optional when existing pressure is sufficient.

psa.footprint_alt: Reference layout drawing for the 40 normal cubic metre per hour PSA nitrogen system
psa.footprint_caption: Reference footprint: approximately 10.17 × 1.60 m. Final footprint and module positions depend on the confirmed supply scope and site conditions.
psa.case_title: On-site nitrogen concept for one 6 kW laser cutter
psa.case_text: This documented layout is presented as a project reference—not as a fixed package for every 6 kW machine. The page shows only the values needed for an initial fit discussion.
psa.inputs_title: What we need before selecting the system
psa.inputs_text: Send operating conditions rather than choosing by flow alone. Final sizing depends on actual duty cycle, gas consumption, ambient conditions and the equipment retained on site.
checklist: Target nitrogen flow, purity and outlet pressure
Laser quantity, power, material range and daily operating hours
Existing compressor, dryer, filters, tanks and booster
Available installation space and utility conditions
Pure-nitrogen cutting or mixed-gas operating plan
psa.boundary_text: The published 40 and 75 Nm³/h values are starting references. A quotation follows a site-condition review; certification scope is not stated on this page until the offered configuration is verified.
psa.faq_title: Questions that change the system scope

faq.question: Do we need to buy the full PSA system?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Suitable compressors, air treatment equipment, tanks or boosters can remain in the project after their capacity and condition are reviewed.

faq.question: Can the PSA system feed pure nitrogen cutting directly?
faq.answer: Yes, when the generated flow, purity and pressure match the cutting requirement. The same nitrogen source can also feed one selected mixed-gas controller when N₂/O₂ mixing is required.

faq.question: Are 40 and 75 Nm³/h the only available capacities?
faq.answer: They are the two reference configurations supported by the current documents. Other requirements must be assessed rather than inferred from an unverified model range.

psa.closing_title: Define the gas demand before defining the equipment list
psa.closing_text: Send your laser load, working hours, required gas conditions and retained plant equipment for a configuration review.

cabinet.fit_text: The cabinet combines the mixed-gas control functions in an external enclosure. Final compatibility still depends on the plant gas sources, pressure, flow, laser demand and installation conditions.

faq.question: Does the cabinet and MSPV2_4000 perform the same function?
faq.answer: Yes. Both control N₂/O₂ mixed gas. The cabinet is a packaged external system; MSPV2_4000 is a compact integration product. They are alternatives, not serial components.

faq.question: Is the cabinet plug-and-play with every laser?
faq.answer: No. Gas sources, pressure, flow, piping, laser demand and site installation must be checked before compatibility is confirmed.

faq.question: What laser powers are covered by the current evidence?
faq.answer: The existing cabinet documentation and site evidence span 6–60 kW applications. That is evidence coverage, not automatic compatibility with every machine in that range.

cabinet.closing_title: Prefer a packaged external mixed-gas system?
cabinet.closing_text: Send the gas-source and cutting conditions so we can check whether the cabinet format matches the project.

valve.title: MSPV2_4000 Compact Mixed-Gas Proportional Valve | GasMixTech

valve.video_description: A rotating product view of the compact N₂/O₂ mixed-gas proportional valve for integration assessment.
valve.lede: N₂/O₂ ratio, pressure and flow control in a compact body for OEM machines, retrofits and space-limited near-process installation.
valve.hero_note: Compact controller · Integration product · Interface and gas-path assessment required

valve.fit_title: Choose compact integration when the customer or OEM can own the surrounding engineering
valve.fit_text: MSPV2_4000 performs the same core mixed-gas function as the cabinet. It requires the integrator to assess enclosure, mounting, wiring, piping, upstream regulation and commissioning.
valve.specs_text: These values belong to MSPV2_4000 and are not evidence for the integrated cabinet.
valve.control_title: Closed-loop feedback adjusts the proportional valve output
valve.control_text: Pressure and flow feedback are compared with the selected targets. The controller drives the valve mechanism to regulate gas ratio, flow and outlet pressure for the specified process.
valve.control_alt: Closed-loop MSPV2_4000 pressure, flow and gas-ratio control principle
valve.installation_title: Compact hardware does not remove the need for gas-path engineering
valve.installation_text: Recommended inlet pressure is 1.5–1.6 MPa, with the N₂/O₂ inlet pressure difference kept within 100 kPa. Upstream regulation, check valves, clean gas, mounting and electrical integration remain part of the project assessment.

valve.faq_title: What must be assessed before integration

faq.question: Is MSPV2_4000 an internal part of the mixing cabinet?
faq.answer: No. MSPV2_4000 and the integrated cabinet are alternative products with the same core N₂/O₂ mixing and output-control function.

faq.question: Do analog and NPN/PNP interfaces mean it fits every laser controller?
faq.answer: No. They are available interface types. Signal definitions, voltage, logic and the complete control sequence must be checked for the target machine.

faq.question: Can we buy MSPV2_4000 directly on DHgate now?
faq.answer: A dedicated product listing is not yet available. The current link opens the SAGEMRO store; use the compatibility inquiry for product-specific assessment.

valve.closing_title: Planning an OEM or retrofit integration?
valve.closing_text: Send the gas conditions, interface plan and installation constraints so we can check whether MSPV2_4000 is the appropriate format.

comparison.title: Integrated Gas Mixing Cabinet vs MSPV2_4000 | Comparison
comparison.description: Compare two alternative N₂/O₂ mixed-gas control products by form factor, published conditions, interfaces and customer integration responsibility.
comparison.lede: Both products perform the same core function: N₂/O₂ mixing with controlled output. Choose one according to installation form, interfaces and the engineering work your team will retain.
comparison.hero_note: Same core function · Alternative products · Never installed as a serial mixer pair
comparison.principle_title: Choose between two product forms—not between high and low grades
comparison.principle_text: The cabinet packages the control function into an external system. MSPV2_4000 concentrates the same core function into a compact integration product. Neither is positioned as newer, better or subordinate to the other.

faq.question: Should the cabinet and MSPV2_4000 be used together?
faq.answer: No. They are alternative mixed-gas controllers. Choose one for the project; do not arrange them as a serial mixer pair.

faq.question: Is MSPV2_4000 the upgraded version of the cabinet?
faq.answer: No. It is a different product form for compact OEM and retrofit integration. The cabinet remains the packaged external option.

faq.question: Which product gives better cutting results?
faq.answer: The current evidence does not support a universal winner. Cutting results depend on the complete machine, gas supply, settings, material and integration conditions.

comparison.closing_title: Send the conditions—we will recommend one format
comparison.closing_text: A short integration review is more useful than selecting by dimensions alone.
